text:
anya: quick sync — ran into a weird class of failures when customers opt into Private but don't deploy the expected sidecar.

matt: ugh, yeah. which failure mode specifically? auth handshake? routing?

anya: mostly controlplane handshake timeouts + config drift causing runtime to reject manifests. We surface as 503 with ambiguous logs.

liam: is this the sidecarless-private pattern we talked about in the RFC? where control plane expects a probe but there's just a passthrough NAT?

anya: exactly. Example sequence: controlplane posts manifest -> sidecar (absent) doesn't bind local port -> runtime never gets the local credential rebind -> controlplane marks tenant unhealthy -> global routing drops to fallback variant.

matt: can you paste a minimal manifest snippet?

anya: sure:
```
manifest: {
  mode: private,
  controlplane_endpoint: https://cp.example,
  local_probe: http://127.0.0.1:4200/ready,
  credential_binding: sidecar://tenant-123
}
```

devx-bot: FYI — saw 12 similar incidents in the last 24h for the eu-west cluster (alert id: DCB-827).

liam: two high-level mitigation ideas: (1) make controlplane handshake tolerant and accept an explicit "sidecar-absent" manifest flag (opt-in), (2) require an async reconciliation probe where runtime can claim "unmanaged-local" and provide a secure long-lived credential backchannel.

matt: tradeoffs? (1) surfaces more complexity to customers and expands manifest surface. (2) needs new backchannel primitives and PKI flows.

anya: yep. Also worried about security: "unmanaged-local" feels like a bigger attack surface if not carefully gated. We need a way to limit scope to tenant-owned networks.

liam: what if we instead provide a small shim binary that runs as a lightweight process (not a k8s sidecar) in private installs? It would handle probe binding and credential exchange with minimal privileges. Call it "rebind-proxy".

matt: advantage: predictable behavior, smaller change to controlplane. downside: ops must install an extra daemon. Also needs packaging for air-gapped installs.

anya: ops-team how heavy is adding a packaged daemon to our private installer vs teaching customers to declare sidecar-absent?

ops-team: packaged daemon is doable. We already ship a small health-exporter for metrics. Adding a signed binary + rpm/deb/arm builds is extra work but manageable. Air-gap support will need zips and clear install instructions.

liam: still need a runtime fallback policy: controlplane should not flip tenant to fallback variant until either (a) rebind-proxy confirmed or (b) a timed grace period expires. Otherwise we churn.

matt: agree. Also add an audit field in the manifest so we can trace why a tenant was downgraded: e.g., downgrade_reason: "probe-missing". Helps SRE & billing disputes.

anya: proposed action items:
- build prototype rebind-proxy (linux amd64 + arm64) and document air-gap install (liam)
- update controlplane handshake to accept a "shim-expected" flag and grace timeout (matt)
- add audit reason and telemetry event for fallback transitions (anya)

liam: I'll spike proxy today. quick question: should the rebind-proxy hold the runtime credential or hand it to runtime?

matt: proxy should perform rebind and hand a minimal token to runtime; token should be scoped and short-lived, rotated via controlplane. Avoid long-lived secrets locally.

ops-team: note: we need KMS integration doc updates for private installs. Pointing to this thread for context.

anya: thanks everyone. If the spike looks good, we'll propose a tiny RFC for the shim pattern and the handshake changes next week. :thumbsup:
